voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: Shugborough Hall, Staffordshire, England. In the mid-seventeen-hundreds, a stone monument was raised in its gardens.
Beneath a carved scene of shepherds at a tomb, eight letters. O, U, O, S, V, A, V, V. And below them, a D and an M.
beats.cap:
O U O S
V A V V

beats.vo: The carving copies a painting by Nicolas Poussin. But in mirror image.
In two thousand four, two veterans of Bletchley Park, Britain's wartime codebreakers, took on the letters. No conclusive answer emerged.
Theories include Latin initials, a private love message, even later graffiti. No reading has ever been accepted.
